title: Absolute Convergence and the Wiener Algebra

items.title: The Wiener algebra of the circle
items.strategy: With the inherited convention T = R/Z, normalized Haar measure, and e_k(x) = exp(2 pi i k x), define A(T) as the integrable functions whose Fourier coefficients are in ell-1(Z), with coefficient ell-1 norm. The next lemma constructs and identifies the continuous representative.

items.title: Absolutely summable Fourier coefficients give uniform convergence
items.strategy: Apply the Weierstrass M-test to sum a_k e_k. Uniform convergence permits termwise integration against e_-m; for f in A(T), the inherited Abel theorem (with its stated ACC hypothesis) converges in L1 to f and uniformly to that synthesis, identifying the continuous representative without assuming Fourier uniqueness.

items.title: The Wiener algebra is a unital commutative Banach algebra
items.strategy: Transport ell-1 completeness through the coefficient bijection established by uniform synthesis. Prove the product-convolution formula first for finite sums, pass by uniform approximation, and apply the ell-1 convolution inequality for the submultiplicative norm bound and unit.

items.title: Weighted ell-2 decay implies absolute convergence
items.strategy: For s > 1/2, apply Cauchy--Schwarz to (a_k) with weights (1+|k|)^s and use convergence of the reciprocal-weight square series. This is a sequence lemma, so it has no planned dependencies.

items.title: A dyadic Fourier-coefficient square-sum bound for Hölder functions
items.strategy: For f in C^alpha(T), choose a translation h comparable to N^-1. Finite character orthogonality applied to f(.-h)-f and a uniform lower bound for |e_k(h)-1| on N <= |k| < 2N give a block ell-2 bound O(N^-2alpha).

items.title: Hölder Fourier coefficients have subcritical weighted ell-2 decay
items.strategy: Sum the preceding dyadic block estimate after multiplying the block at scale N by N^(2s). The resulting geometric series converges for every 0 < s < alpha, giving the weighted ell-2 bridge required by Bernstein's theorem.

items.title: Bernstein's absolute-convergence theorem
items.strategy: For 1/2 < alpha <= 1, choose s strictly between 1/2 and alpha. The Hölder weighted ell-2 lemma supplies the hypothesis of the Cauchy--Schwarz lemma, so f belongs to A(T). State C^alpha using the circular distance and its usual Hölder modulus.

items.title: Periodic L2 weak derivative on the circle
items.strategy: For f and g in L2(T), define g as the periodic weak derivative of f when the integral of f times every smooth periodic test derivative equals minus the integral of g times the test function. Treat both functions as almost-everywhere classes and fix T = R/Z.

items.title: Fourier coefficients of a periodic weak derivative
items.strategy: Insert the smooth character e_-k into the periodic weak-derivative identity. With the library convention e_k(x) = exp(2 pi i k x), obtain hat(g)(k) = 2 pi i k hat(f)(k), checking k = 0 separately.

items.title: One ell-2 weak derivative implies an absolutely convergent Fourier series
items.strategy: Use the local periodic weak-derivative coefficient identity, derive the finite weighted ell-2 estimate by character orthogonality, and apply the weighted Cauchy--Schwarz lemma with s = 1.

items.title: Wiener's lemma for absolutely convergent Fourier series
items.strategy: Prove the source-backed inverse-closedness theorem for A(T): identify its coefficient algebra with ell-one of the integers, compute the characters as evaluation on the circle, and apply the commutative Banach-algebra invertibility criterion to a nowhere-zero function.

items.title: Holomorphic functional calculus in the Wiener algebra
items.strategy: For a function holomorphic on a neighborhood of the range of f in A(T), combine the Cauchy integral formula with the locally proved inverse-closedness theorem; approximate the resulting A(T)-valued contour integral by Riemann sums to conclude that the holomorphic composition remains in A(T).

title: Absolute Convergence and the Wiener Algebra — Examples

items.title: A trigonometric polynomial in the Wiener algebra
items.strategy: Use an explicit finite Fourier polynomial and compute its A(T) norm as the finite sum of the moduli of its displayed coefficients.

items.title: An absolutely convergent Fourier series that is not twice continuously differentiable
items.strategy: For f(x) = sum over k nonzero of |k|^-2 e_k(x), use comparison for A(T). If f were C^2, two integrations by parts would make the Fourier coefficients of f'' a nonzero constant away from zero, contradicting the Riemann--Lebesgue lemma.

items.title: Continuity does not imply absolute Fourier convergence
items.strategy: Use the continuous C^(1/2) function outside A(T) supplied by the cited endpoint construction. State only the resulting existence counterexample, making clear that continuity alone does not force ell-1 Fourier coefficients.

items.title: The Bernstein Hölder-one-half endpoint can fail
items.strategy: Use Grafakos's stated exponential-sum estimate to obtain a function in Lambda^(1/2)(T) outside A(T). Preserve the source qualification that the exponential-sum estimate itself is assumed without proof.

items.title: Wiener inversion needs nonvanishing
items.strategy: The polynomial 1 - e_1 belongs to A(T) but vanishes at the identity. Its pointwise reciprocal cannot be continuous, hence cannot be a member of A(T), showing the nonvanishing hypothesis is indispensable.
